text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock rose nearly 1% today to close at $390.78, capping a strong two-week rally of over 9%. The gain reflects escalating geopolitical tension in the Middle East—Iran struck Kuwait on Thursday, pushing Brent crude above $96 per barrel and U.S. oil to $91.48—combined with U.S. refineries running at 98% capacity utilization. For a refiner, higher oil prices and tight refinery operations both drive profitability: refineries earn more when they're fully utilized, and geopolitical premium in crude prices can widen margins if product demand stays strong.

The broader momentum fits a clear pattern: oil prices have gained more than 7% this week alone as military escalation between the U.S. and Iran continues. With storage levels moderate (gasoline and diesel inventories neither depleted nor bloated) and refineries already maxed out, the market is pricing in sustained tight conditions, which benefits refiners' bottom lines as long as crude prices stay elevated and geopolitical risk keeps buyers nervous.
